# Phobos Framework: equipment and item reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/update-item-reference.ps1. Edit config/item-reference.json, not this file. -->

Current source candidate: **0.100.0**. Game target: **1.0.1.5**. Values below come from offline definitions; they do not establish installation, gameplay validation or a live merchant quote.

Framework supplies shared services rather than a set of standalone machines. Since 0.57.0 it also owns the two lines every Phobos mod shares, the gas line and the process-water line, so any mod's machines can pipe to any mod's stores. Repairs on every Phobos machine use up their parts, as the game's own repairs do; the retired spent service parts are listed for older saves. Construction menus, machinery controls and the opt-in Scope recorder are interfaces, not additional inventory objects. Crew standing orders are opt-in; see [crew work, training and time-skips](crew-automation.md) for eligible work, approved stores, resource limits and resuming industrial and exterior work. Compact controls, unsaved settings and object selection are explained in the [control-panel guide](control-panel-guide.md). In selection fields, Locate opens a temporary marked ship view; Clear is a draft change that requires Apply. Pick on ship marks eligible objects and Escape restores the panel and view.

**Reading prices:** credits per complete object at the stated condition, before shop margins, market effects, negotiation and extra wear. Pristine retail can cost more. Mass is the empty/dry definition or fresh commodity template; saved contents and variable recovery packets can weigh differently. Dismantle value is the sum of all listed outputs at base value, excluding labour and tools.

**Repair and Restore:** Repair fixes a damaged form and uses up its parts, as the game's own repairs do. Restore reduces wear on functional equipment in place; it does not grant pristine status. Empty cargo and follow the machine’s local maintenance guards first. Work speed depends on crew, tools and current condition.

**Finding stock:** the generated percentages are defaults per eligible native stock/loot roll, not per ship or guaranteed shop availability. Offers are additive, may be independent, and require normal restocking. Merchant offers request the listed finite lot when successful; separate world-loot branches retain their own listed quantities. Configuration, capacity and native generation rules still apply; loading an existing save does not refill its inventories.

**Stacking:** limits below apply to loose items on the ground or in compatible containers; 1 means no multi-item stack. Installed equipment remains individual. Limits count objects, not kilograms, and do not change merchant lot sizes or per-object contents.

<a id="spent-service-parts"></a>

## Spent Service Parts

Legacy, retired in Framework 0.74.0: worn parts that Phobos repairs used to leave behind. Repairs now use up their parts, as the game's own repairs do.

**Use:** Nothing to do: any left in a save are removed when the ship loads, with one crew-log line.

**Where it appears:** Only in saves from before Framework 0.74.0. Nothing makes them any more.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

The definition stays registered only so older saves load them before they are removed.

Full operating instructions: [Spent Service Parts guide](equipment-economy.md).

<a id="gas-line"></a>

## Gas line

Sealed Fennmark gas line joining gas stores and the machines that fill or draw from them: Manufacturing's stores, V4, X2, K2, AX-2, LC-3, SA-3, P1, L2 and A2, and Shipbreaker's T2 for methane. Every gas store and gas-using machine the line runs under or right beside joins one network, and touching equipment joins without it. It has its own lane, so it shares tiles with other lines. Its retained waste is what dismantling leaves.

**Use:** Lay it through INSTALL > HVAC on intact floor until it runs under or right beside each machine and store, on any side. Link choices say why a store aboard is not offered. A damaged segment breaks the network there until repaired. To take it up, right-click it and choose Vent gas line; the run closes until Return line to service.

**Where it appears:** Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson and the Venus scrap kiosk in lots of 128. Ordinary supply. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → HVAC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Moved from Manufacturing to Framework in 0.57.0 with its saved identity, name, price and bills unchanged, so it no longer needs Manufacturing installed. Since Framework 0.63.0 it holds a few grams of gas a tile, a mix when several gases share it, filled from its stores; a damaged segment lets its gas into the room (hydrogen overboard), and a segment holding gas cannot be taken up until vented. Pressure drop is neglected. When an oxygen store and a fuel store share one line, the stores' panels and the crew log say so; nothing is blocked. The retained waste is terminal.

Full operating instructions: [Gas line guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="water-line"></a>

## Process water line

Sealed line for process water between water tanks (Framework's Rivetline silos, and Ship's Water 0.16.1 tanks when installed) and the machines that draw or make water: Manufacturing's V4, X2, K2, LC-3 and SA-3, Shipbreaker's T2 and Agriculture's W2 intake and racks. Every water tank and water-using machine the line runs under or right beside joins one network, and touching equipment joins without it. It has its own blue lane, so it shares tiles with other lines.

**Use:** Lay it through INSTALL > HVAC on intact floor until it runs under or right beside each machine and tank, on any side. Then link the machine to the tank on its Control Panel; the list shows how each tank is reached. To take it up, right-click it and choose Drain line into canister with a drain canister carried or within two tiles; the run closes until Return line to service.

**Where it appears:** Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson and the Venus scrap kiosk in lots of 128. Ordinary supply. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → HVAC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

New in Framework 0.57.0. Process grade only: it never joins drinking water. Since Framework 0.63.0 it holds about 0.49 kg of water a tile, filled from its tanks (and, since Framework 0.65.0, from Ship’s Water drinking tanks above the crew reserve), and a segment holding water cannot be taken up until drained. Irrigation conduit is a separate line for the W2's racks. The retained waste is terminal.

Full operating instructions: [Process water line guide](manufacturing-player-guide.md).

<a id="conveyor-belt"></a>

## Rivetline conveyor belt

Conveyor belt for loose items between machines, collectors and stores. A run of intact belt that lies on or beside two pieces of equipment joins them for Phobos Shipbreaker's item routes: a collector fed by a D4, the reclaimer's feed, the F6's input and output, and D4 or R4 storage output. Equipment within one tile of each other needs no belt.

**Use:** Lay it through INSTALL > MISC on intact floor, tile by tile, from beside the sender to beside the receiver: a machine's footprint, a collector's inboard tiles or the F6's input or output marker. Then link and start the route; its status says whether it runs by conveyor belt or touching. Belts share tiles with pipe and line, in the lowest lane.

**Where it appears:** Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson and the Venus scrap kiosk in lots of 128. Ordinary supply. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → MISC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

New in Framework 0.61.0. Items never ride it: each still moves straight from one machine to the other in one checked transfer, powered and paid for by the machine that sends or receives it. A belt cut, damaged or taken up stops the route until you mend it and resume. Dismantling returns the whole segment as retained waste, which is terminal.

Full operating instructions: [Rivetline conveyor belt guide](automatic-material-routing.md).

<a id="drain-canister"></a>

## Rivetline D20 drain canister

A portable 20 litre lined can for draining lines: about 20 kg of water or 36.7 kg of sulfuric acid, one liquid at a time. It carries a drained line’s contents back to a tank.

**Use:** Carry it, or leave it on the deck within two tiles of the line, then right-click an installed water or acid line and choose Drain line into canister. Haul the full canister into the inventory of a tank that holds the same liquid (a Rivetline water silo, or an acid tank’s canister rack) and it pours in, leaving the empty can there. The game’s own Haul orders or a hauling mod such as Common Sense move it like any cargo.

**Where it appears:** Sold new at the K-Leg supply kiosk and fixer, San Diego Halvorson, the Venus scrap kiosk and the regional supply kiosks in lots of 16. Ordinary supply. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

New in Framework 0.63.0. It never stacks, since each canister records what it holds; its weight is the 3 kg can plus that liquid. Gas lines are vented instead, since they hold only grams. No repair or dismantling. Its sprite is PixelLab art since Framework 0.65.0.

Full operating instructions: [Rivetline D20 drain canister guide](lines-and-draining.md).

<a id="water-tanks"></a>

## S2, S3, S4 and S5 Process Water Silos

Passive vessels holding process water as a saved record, shared by every Phobos mod: the 2 x 2 S2 holds 400 kg, the 3 x 3 S3 1,000 kg, the 4 x 4 S4 1,960 kg and the 5 x 5 S5 3,330 kg. Bigger silos hold more for less per kilogram of capacity; a full silo weighs its housing plus its water. Each has a four-cell service rack for manual work.

**Use:** Install through APPS; no power. Machines reach a silo by touching it or along a process-water line that runs under or right beside both, and several machines can share one. Fill at a station under Bulk supplies, from a linked machine such as a T2, or (with Ship's Water 0.16.1) draw from the drinking-water tanks above the crew reserve; send water to the waste tanks for the Recycler. With Agriculture, crew can load 5 kg irrigation charges from its inventory, drain it or keep it topped up by standing order. Set Keep in reserve on the panel or C1; a refuelling kiosk buys water above the reserve back at 4.50 cr/kg under Bulk supplies. After damage, repair and Recover trapped water; a protected silo offers Accept contents as they are. See [the silo guide](shipbreaker-bulk-silos.md).

**Where it appears:** Buy loose hardware from the sellers below. No fabrication recipe. The S3 may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; the S2, S4 and S5 do not. See the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Moved from Shipbreaker to Framework in Framework 0.58.0 with their ids, saved records and names unchanged; the S2 is new, and Agriculture's retired R3, R4 and R5 reservoirs convert to the S3, S4 and S5 on load. Process water only: never a drinking-water tank, never fuel. Uninstalling carries the water with the loose silo; Dismantle is refused while water remains, and removal is refused while the silo is protected. Water is lost with a destroyed silo (logged). The S2's sprite is a recorded reduction of the S3's.

Full operating instructions: [S2, S3, S4 and S5 Process Water Silos guide](shipbreaker-bulk-silos.md).

## Evidence and upkeep

Item names, dry/template masses, prices, service bills, salvage outputs, placement tabs, stock probabilities and table recipes are generated from current Phobos definitions. **Blue Bottle Games’ Ostranauts** native `DataCO.GetBasePrice` supplies the offline valuation used here ([developer’s game page](https://bluebottlegames.com/games/ostranauts)). That page identifies the game; the actual numeric evidence is the locally inspected assembly, whose hash is retained in the generated data snapshot. No proprietary source or game assembly is distributed.

Function/use explanations are maintained in the reviewed catalogue. All fictional prices, yields and simplified processing are Phobos gameplay choices. Research attribution remains beside the relevant claims in the linked operating/research guides. See [reference maintenance](development/item-reference-maintenance.md) for the one-click updater and coverage checks.
